parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal statute, no cross-dressing ban, no documented border, bathroom or custody rule aimed at visitors: the state does not impose universal exposure on travellers. Same-sex conduct is lawful and a national human-rights council publicly defended woubis and lelés in 2024. But the worst documented feature is tier-3: societal hostility with effectively no recourse. Trans-feminine and visibly gender-nonconforming people are singled out; 45 anti-LGBTQ assaults were recorded in the largest city in two months of 2024 after influencer incitement; police are slow and victim-blaming; there is no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection; healthcare refusal and forced prayer-camp 'therapy' are documented. Dated 2010–2012 security-force raids show state actors as past perpetrators. No visitor-specific evidence exists either way, so the rating extrapolates from the local pattern and the absent protective machinery rather than resolving to the midpoint.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific border rule, marker-mismatch practice or entry refusal documented. Article 360's aggravated same-sex decency provision exists but has no record of use at crossings.
entry_documents.interaction: How officers treat a passport whose marker conflicts with presentation is unresolved; no visitor case is sourced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No criminalisation of trans identity or expression. Custody placement and treatment of trans detainees wholly unsourced. Dated 2010–2012 security-force raids on a queer bar, with forced undressing and extorted fines, show state actors as past perpetrators.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Whether a document discrepancy could escalate into police holding, and where a trans detainee would be placed, is unanswered by any source.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, changing-room, ward-placement or single-sex-facility rule reaching trans visitors appears in the record.

care_services.exposure: Healthcare discrimination documented, including refusal of service; conversion therapy reported in 2023, with a transgender man forced to a prayer camp attempting suicide afterwards.
care_services.protection: Non-discrimination in health promised in 2010 as a general commitment only, with no operative remedy shown.
care_services.interaction: A trans visitor needing care or medication abroad faces discretionary refusal with no anti-discrimination route to challenge it.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: In 2024 influencers exhorted followers to attack gender-nonconforming people and a market attack followed; the president pledged a bill to 'counter the expansion' of homosexuality (outcome unsourced). Police responses slow, ineffective and often victim-blaming.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: September 2024 National Human Rights Council statement affirming constitutional and treaty rights of woubis and lelés, calling for an end to online hate.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetorical hostility raises both discovery-linked risk and the chance that a complaint is dismissed or turned against the complainant.

minors_guardians.exposure: Age of consent 18 for same-sex couples versus 15 for different-sex; decency penalties doubled where a minor is present or involved; school dropout from family expulsion documented. No facility or custody rule for trans minors sourced.
minors_guardians.protection: None documented for minors; schools show no anti-discrimination coverage.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a gender-nonconforming minor has no documented recourse if staff, hosts or police treat the child's presentation as a decency matter.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 45 assault incidents against LGBTQ people in the largest city in two months of 2024; a transgender man beaten in Abobo; 2023 official report records community deaths and describes police as slow, ineffective and victim-blaming. Trans-feminine people face elevated risk because presentation breaches norms.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Authorities described as handling complaints somewhat better than before; no enforcement outcome against attackers is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Wealthier people are treated with less hostility, which partially shields some visitors; visible trans-feminine presentation attracts the documented targeting.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law and no sourced hate-crime provision; many victims do not report, believing police will not act. No visitor-facing complaint mechanism documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: NHRC advocacy and constitutional/treaty language only; no remedy shown to operate in practice.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: An assaulted visitor would rely on a police service the record describes as victim-blaming, with no civil-rights fallback.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-B has police systematically stopping trans visitors, confiscating documents and holding them for hours under a formal bylaw. Nothing comparable is documented here: no stop practice, no visitor detention, no official file. This jurisdiction is therefore higher, since its exposure is societal with episodic state failure rather than a routine state campaign.

0.55-A imposes universal visitor registration and checkpoint holding, but documents no pattern of beatings and offers a legal-aid clinic. Here there is no state registration machinery, yet a recent multi-dozen assault wave, trans-specific targeting and no recourse. Lower than 0.55-A: unregulated street hostility outweighs bureaucratic friction.

0.75-C has trained border officers, brief detention ending in release, written reasons, counsel and compensation through a tribunal. This jurisdiction documents none of that protective machinery and shows police inaction instead of remedy, placing it far below.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is one of legal non-criminalisation of same-sex conduct alongside the absence of any gender-identity protection, plus a decency statute whose aggravated same-sex limb is available but not shown to be used against visitors. There is no documented state-imposed traveller exposure — no border rule, facility ban, registration or custody practice is sourced — which keeps the score out of the severe band. What moves it down is a documented, recent pattern of anti-LGBTQ assault and incitement concentrated on visibly gender-nonconforming and trans-feminine people, with police described as slow and victim-blaming and no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse on the books. The unresolved items — custody placement, border document handling, the fate of the promised bill — are open questions, not established exposures, and carry accordingly less weight than the documented violence and absent remedies.
